turns.user: Tin tức AI hôm nay có gì nổi bật?
turns.assistant_text:
Dưới đây là một số tin tức nổi bật về AI hôm nay:

1. **AI không thể được cấp phép như bác sĩ**: Hiệp hội Y khoa Hoa Kỳ (AMA) đã thông qua chính sách mới khẳng định rằng AI có thể hỗ trợ bác sĩ trong các nhiệm vụ lâm sàng nhưng không thể được cấp phép hành nghề y. Điều này nhấn mạnh tầm quan trọng của sự minh bạch và giám sát của bác sĩ khi AI được tích hợp vào quy trình chăm sóc sức khỏe. [Đọc thêm](https://www.ama-assn.org/practice-management/digital-health/who-can-be-licensed-physician-not-ai).

2. **Xây dựng khả năng hiểu biết về AI**: Các giảng viên tại Đại học Bang Washington đang thảo luận về việc nâng cao khả năng hiểu biết về AI cho sinh viên thông qua các hội thảo và podcast, nhằm giúp sinh viên không chỉ sử dụng AI mà còn hiểu rõ hơn về nó. [Đọc thêm](https://news.wsu.edu/news/2026/11/10/nov-18-carson-faculty-discuss-building-ai-literacy-on-adobe-podcast).

3. **Ý kiến về video AI**: Một bài viết trên Washington Post chia sẻ quan điểm cá nhân về việc sản xuất video AI, mặc dù không được đánh giá cao, nhưng tác giả vẫn cảm thấy thú vị khi làm việc với chúng. [Đọc thêm](https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2026/11/10/ai-videos-are-not-well-regarded-im-still-making-them-anyway).

4. **Thị trường hoán đổi tín dụng và AI**: Sự gia tăng đầu tư vào AI đã làm nổi bật thị trường hoán đổi tín dụng, nơi các CFO cần theo dõi để hiểu cách các nhà đầu tư đánh giá rủi ro tín dụng của họ. [Đọc thêm](https://www.wsj.com/cfo-journal/why-the-credit-default-swap-marketred-hot-in-the-ai-tradeis-vital-for-cfos-9a8aac4a).

5. **Scandal của CEO Nvidia và cuộc đua AI Mỹ-Trung**: Cổ phiếu của Nvidia giảm do scandal liên quan đến CEO Jensen Huang, người bị nghi ngờ có quan hệ với một phụ nữ có khả năng làm gián điệp cho Trung Quốc, điều này có thể ảnh hưởng đến cuộc đua AI giữa Mỹ và Trung Quốc. [Đọc thêm](https://www.wbur.org/hereandnow/2026/11/10/nvidia-ceo-ai-race).

Nếu bạn cần thêm thông tin chi tiết về bất kỳ tin tức nào, hãy cho tôi biết!

items.title: Who can be licensed as a physician? Not AI | American Medical Association
items.summary: The AMA is drawing a clear line between augmented intelligence (AI) as a tool to support healthcare and the practice of medicine. AI—often called artificial intelligence—can help doctors with clinical tasks, but it cannot be granted physician licensure, professional titles or certification to practice medicine, says new policy adopted at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting. [...] “AI can help physicians analyze information, identify patterns and support clinical decision-making, but patients deserve to know who is responsible for their care,” said AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH. “Physicians also need the authority, oversight and liability protections to make independent decisions when AI is part of the care team.” [...] Transparency and physician-led oversight are needed as hospitals and health systems increasingly incorporate augmented intelligence (AI) into administrative and governance workflows, as well as emerging applications that support credentialing, privileging, peer review, quality review and other professional practices evaluation processes, says a separate resolution that was introduced at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting.

items.title: Why the Credit Default Swap Market—Red Hot in the AI Trade—Is Vital for CFOs - WSJ
items.summary:
The rush by investors to take out insurance on their massive AI trades has put a spotlight on a market that CFOs rely on for signals about how investors perceive them. [...] CDS spreads—the price investors pay for the insurance—have widened for AI companies relative to the broader market index. “At a high level, spreads appear to be inconsistent with the large market caps in the equity market,” Patel said, pointing to hyperscalers’ size. Investors need to be compensated for the uncertainty surrounding companies’ AI funding needs, he said.

Copyright ©2026 Dow Jones & Company, Inc. All Rights Reserved. 87990cbe856818d5eddac44c7b1cdeb8 [...] Investors use credit default swaps to hedge existing exposure to an issuer, or to express a view on its credit risk without necessarily holding its debt. Following a massive borrowing spree by hyperscalers to build out AI infrastructure, market participants have taken out more protection on their trades against borrower default. That means buying more CDS contracts.

items.title: Why the Credit Default Swap Market—Red Hot in the AI Trade—Is Vital for CFOs - WSJ
items.summary:
The rush by investors to take out insurance on their massive AI trades has put a spotlight on a market that CFOs rely on for signals about how investors perceive them. [...] CDS spreads—the price investors pay for the insurance—have widened for AI companies relative to the broader market index. “At a high level, spreads appear to be inconsistent with the large market caps in the equity market,” Patel said, pointing to hyperscalers’ size. Investors need to be compensated for the uncertainty surrounding companies’ AI funding needs, he said.

Copyright ©2026 Dow Jones & Company, Inc. All Rights Reserved. 87990cbe856818d5eddac44c7b1cdeb8 [...] Investors use credit default swaps to hedge existing exposure to an issuer, or to express a view on its credit risk without necessarily holding its debt. Following a massive borrowing spree by hyperscalers to build out AI infrastructure, market participants have taken out more protection on their trades against borrower default. That means buying more CDS contracts.

items.title: What Nvidia CEO's alleged spy scandal means for the U.S.-China AI race | Here & Now
items.summary:
Nvidia's stock price continues to slump as a scandal involving CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman suspected of spying for China unfolds.

Here & Now's Robin Young speaks with Matt Sheehan, co-director of the China AI Initiative at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, about the broader implications for the U.S.-China artificial intelligence race.

This segment aired on November 10, 2026.
